abstract: The insatiable energy and throughput demands of deep neural network inference have pushed digital electronic accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward severe thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. All-Optical Neural Networks (ONNs) and Diffractive Deep Learning establish a revolutionary computing paradigm that executes massive matrix-vector multiplications and spatial classification tasks at the speed of light in free space with near-zero runtime electrical power dissipation. By structuring multi-layer cascades of sub-wavelength dielectric metasurfaces, diffractive deep neural networks (D2NNs) modulate incoming optical wavefront amplitudes and phases through passive light propagation, naturally performing linear matrix transformations via Huygens-Fresnel diffraction principles. However, translating all-optical diffractive processors from theoretical simulations into robust hardware accelerators introduces profound physical and manufacturing bottlenecks: severe fabrication tolerances in sub-wavelength nano-antennas, limited angular and wavelength tolerances, insertion loss accumulation across deep multi-layer diffractive stacks, and the challenge of implementing non-linear optical activations without electrical domain conversion. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of diffractive deep learning and alloptical neural networks. We formalize scalar diffraction theory via Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation integrals, derive dielectric metasurface phase modulation transfer functions, and model optical backpropagation training via adjointvariable gradient methods. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise multi-physics co-simulation and physical optical testbed evaluating 5-layer stacked silicon nitride (Si3N4) metasurface diffractive processors across multi-class image classification (Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10) and optical vortex mode sorting. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our all-optical diffractive processor achieves 94.8% classification accuracy on Fashion-MNIST while executing inference in 33 picoseconds (speed of light propagation delay) with an active operational energy dissipation of 0.17 attojoules per classification - outperforming 4nm digital CMOS accelerators by over five orders of magnitude in energy efficiency. Finally, we formulate open challenges in all-optical non-linear activation materials, reconfigurable dynamic spatial light modulators, and multi-wavelength broadband diffractive multiplexing.
authors: Ujjwal Kukreja, Amit Singh Bhati, Dr. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr. Ashok Kajla

abstract: Abstract Research into optical spiking neural networks (SNNs) has primarily focused on spiking devices, networks of excitable lasers or numerical modeling of large architectures, often overlooking key constraints such as limited optical power, crosstalk and footprint. We introduce SEPhIA, a photonic-electronic, multi-tiled SNN architecture emphasizing implementation feasibility and realistic scaling. SEPhIA leverages microring modulators (MRMs) and multi-wavelength sources to achieve effective $$ < 1$$ < 1 laser-per-spiking neuron ratio. We validate SEPhIA at both device and architecture levels by time‑domain co‑simulating excitable CMOS‑MRM coupled circuits and by devising a physics‑aware, trainable optoelectronic SNN model, with both approaches utilizing experimentally derived device parameters. The multi-layer optoelectronic SNN achieves classification accuracies over 90% on a four-class spike-encoded dataset, closely comparable to software models. A design space study further quantifies how photonic device parameters impact SNN performance under constrained signal-to-noise conditions. SEPhIA offers a scalable, expressive, physically grounded solution for neuromorphic photonic computing, capable of addressing spike-encoded tasks.
title: SEPhIA: spiking electro-photonic integrated tiled architecture leveraging multi-wavelength lasers for scalable optical neuromorphic computing
